event_title: Ekiti State created from Ondo State
description: Ekiti State was carved out of Ondo State with Ado-Ekiti as capital. According to the state government it was created alongside five other states and started with 16 Local Government Areas.
source: Ekiti State Government: About Ekiti
notes_limitations: Two official pages agree on the date. The state website's population figures for this period differ from other sources (see the 2006 census entry).

event_title: Col. Mohammed Bawa becomes first military administrator
description: Colonel Mohammed Bawa was appointed the first Administrator of Ekiti State under the Abacha regime and served until August 1998.
source: Wikipedia: Mohammed Bawa
notes_limitations: Wikipedia gives 7 Oct 1996 as start date. Replace with the state's official list of past governors or a gazette. Earlier drafts wrongly gave his rank as Lt. Col.

event_title: Navy Capt. Atanda Yusuf becomes administrator
description: Navy Captain (retd) Musbau Atanda Yusuf succeeded Bawa during the Abubakar transition and served until civilian rule began on 29 May 1999.
source: Wikipedia: Atanda Yusuf
notes_limitations: Needs confirmation from the state's past-governors page or a gazette.

event_title: Federal Medical Centre, Ido-Ekiti founded
description: The Federal Medical Centre in Ido-Ekiti, later upgraded to a teaching hospital, is recorded as founded in 1998.
source: Wikipedia: Federal Teaching Hospital, Ido Ekiti
notes_limitations: Confirm founding year on the hospital's own site (fethi.gov.ng) or a federal source.

event_title: Civilian rule returns: Niyi Adebayo sworn in as first elected governor
description: Otunba Niyi Adebayo of the Alliance for Democracy served as Ekiti's first elected civilian governor from 29 May 1999 to 29 May 2003.
source: Wikipedia: Niyi Adebayo
notes_limitations: Dates appear consistently across reference sites, but a primary source is still needed.

event_title: State House of Assembly complex inaugurated
description: The complex housing the Ekiti State House of Assembly, built during Atanda Yusuf's tenure as administrator, was inaugurated by Governor Adebayo.
source: Wikipedia: Atanda Yusuf (citing ThisDay, 9 Jan 2010)
notes_limitations: Find the original ThisDay article or an Assembly source.

event_title: Ayo Fayose becomes governor (first term)
description: Ayo Fayose of the PDP defeated Niyi Adebayo and took office on 29 May 2003.
source: THISDAY: The Judiciary as an Impediment (2017)
notes_limitations: Start date from Wikipedia: Ayo Fayose.

event_title: National population census conducted; Ekiti totals reported differently
description: The 2006 national census was conducted between 21 and 27 March 2006, with final results gazetted in 2009. Sources give three different totals for Ekiti State.
source: Federal Government of Nigeria Gazette (2 Feb 2009)
notes_limitations: Ekiti State Government says 2,384,212; CityPopulation (citing NPC/NBS) shows 2,398,957; Wikipedia shows 2,210,957. Obtain the NPC state table before publishing any figure.

event_title: Governor Fayose impeached by the House of Assembly
description: The House of Assembly impeached Fayose and his deputy, Biodun Olujimi, in controversial circumstances about seven months before his first term ended.
source: SaharaReporters (15 Oct 2006)
notes_limitations: Exact date differs: 15 Oct (contemporaneous report, THISDAY) versus 16 Oct (Naija News, citing state records). In April 2015 the Supreme Court held impeachment is not a ground for disqualification.

event_title: State of emergency declared; Tunji Olurin appointed sole administrator
description: President Obasanjo declared a state of emergency in Ekiti, suspended the governor, deputy and Assembly, and appointed Tunji Olurin. The National Assembly ratified it on 26 Oct 2006.
source: Wikipedia: Tunji Olurin
notes_limitations: Replace with a Presidency or National Assembly source.

event_title: Tope Ademiluyi becomes acting governor
description: Olurin's tenure ended on 27 April 2007 and Tope Ademiluyi served as acting governor until the May handover.
source: Wikipedia: Tunji Olurin
notes_limitations: ZODML lists Apr-May 2007 for Ademiluyi. Needs a primary source.

event_title: Segun Oni sworn in as governor
description: Segun Oni of the PDP, declared winner of the April 2007 election, was sworn in on 29 May 2007. Kayode Fayemi challenged the result at the tribunal.
source: THISDAY: The Judiciary as an Impediment (2017)

event_title: Afe Babalola University established in Ado-Ekiti
description: Afe Babalola University (ABUAD), a private non-profit university founded by Afe Babalola, was established in Ado-Ekiti.
source: Times Higher Education: Afe Babalola University profile
notes_limitations: Year confirmed by the university, THE and the IAU/WHED directory.

event_title: Court of Appeal ends Oni's tenure; Kayode Fayemi sworn in
description: On 15 Oct 2010 the Court of Appeal sitting in Kwara State declared Fayemi the duly elected governor of the 2007 election, ending Oni's term. Fayemi was sworn in on 16 Oct 2010.
source: Ekiti State Government: Fayemi's Care For The Aged In Ekiti
notes_limitations: Swearing-in date from the state website; court date from Wikipedia and THISDAY.

event_title: Rehabilitation of Ikogosi Warm Springs Resort begins
description: The Fayemi administration began rehabilitating the Ikogosi Warm Springs Resort, which had suffered years of neglect.
source: Ekiti State Government: The re-birth of Ikogosi Warm Springs Resort
notes_limitations: Official article dated 4 Aug 2012. History of the site: Baptist camp from 1952; Ondo State acquired it in 1978 (AJLA Journal).

event_title: University of Ado-Ekiti renamed Ekiti State University
description: The University of Ado-Ekiti (1999-2011) became Ekiti State University (EKSU). The institution began in 1982 as Obafemi Awolowo University, Ado-Ekiti.
source: Ekiti State University: About EKSU
notes_limitations: 2011 rename per Wikipedia; the university's own page covers the earlier history.

event_title: Federal University Oye-Ekiti established
description: Federal University Oye-Ekiti (FUOYE) was founded by the federal government with campuses at Oye-Ekiti and Ikole-Ekiti; first graduating set in 2015.
source: Wikipedia: Federal University Oye Ekiti
notes_limitations: Confirm with the university site (fuoye.edu.ng) or the Federal Ministry of Education.

event_title: Ekiti launches Social Security Scheme for the elderly
description: Payments of N5,000 monthly to indigent citizens aged 65 and above began on 25 Oct 2011, starting with about 10,000 beneficiaries at Ise-Ekiti and later rising to around 20,000.
source: Ekiti State Government: Ekiti Marks 2nd Anniversary Of Social Security For Elderly Citizens
notes_limitations: Several official articles agree on the date. Claims that it was the first scheme of its kind in Nigeria, West Africa or sub-Saharan Africa are government statements and are not independently verified.

event_title: Social Security Scheme backed by law
description: Governor Fayemi signed the Social Security bill into law, giving the elderly-stipend scheme legal backing after about six months of operation.
source: Ekiti State Government: Fayemi Signs Social Security Bill To Law
notes_limitations: Article is dated 18 Mar 2012 and says the signing was 'Friday', which points to 16 Mar 2012.

event_title: Redeveloped Ikogosi resort opened to the public
description: The refurbished resort was opened to the public in October 2012 as part of the marking of Fayemi's second year in office. Full operations were announced for April 2013.
source: Ekiti State Government: Ikogosi Warm Spring Resort feature
notes_limitations: Year inferred from 'second year in office'. Feb 2013 (ready for commissioning) and Mar 2013 (full operation in April) articles give supporting context.

event_title: Ekiti Knowledge Zone conceived
description: The Ekiti Knowledge Zone (EKZ), a technology and innovation hub, was conceived on 12 Aug 2013 under Governor Fayemi, according to Governor Oyebanji.
source: Ekiti State Government: EKZ sod-turning report
notes_limitations: Date is from the governor's statement; TechCabal independently dates the blueprint to 2013. Earlier drafts wrongly said 2019.

event_title: Fayose defeats incumbent Fayemi in governorship election
description: Ayo Fayose won the 2014 governorship election, defeating the incumbent Kayode Fayemi.
source: THISDAY: The Judiciary as an Impediment (2017)
notes_limitations: Election date from Wikipedia: Kayode Fayemi. Confirm against INEC.

event_title: Ayo Fayose sworn in for second term
description: Fayose's second term ran from 16 Oct 2014 to 16 Oct 2018.
source: Wikipedia: Ayo Fayose
notes_limitations: THISDAY (2017) confirms Oct 2014.

event_title: Supreme Court upholds Fayose's 2014 victory
description: The Supreme Court held that impeachment was not a ground for disqualification from contesting governorship again, ending the challenge to Fayose's election.
source: THISDAY: The Judiciary as an Impediment (2017)
notes_limitations: Secondary reports date the ruling to 14 Apr 2015. Some commentary says the court also found he was not validly impeached; the THISDAY article states only the disqualification finding.

event_title: Ekiti State Health Insurance Scheme law signed
description: The state government states it signed into law the bill establishing the Ekiti State Health Insurance Scheme to give residents equitable access to basic health care.
source: Ekiti State Government: Ekiti Health Insurance Scheme page
notes_limitations: Month and day not given. In Feb 2021 the state was still describing the scheme as being rolled out.

event_title: Anti-open grazing law signed
description: Governor Fayose signed the Prohibition of Cattle and Other Ruminants Grazing in Ekiti Law, 2016, restricting grazing to 7am-6pm and designated areas and treating armed grazing as terrorism, after an attack in Oke-Ako, Ikole LGA.
source: Ripples Nigeria: Fayose's anti-grazing law stirs controversy
notes_limitations: Date confirmed by several outlets. The law was contested and enforcement was reported as uneven.

event_title: ABUAD Teaching Hospital (400 beds) commissioned
description: The 400-bed Afe Babalola University Teaching Hospital in Ado-Ekiti was commissioned by then Vice President Yemi Osinbajo.
source: Wikipedia: Afe Babalola University Teaching Hospital
notes_limitations: Find a news report or the university's own announcement.

event_title: Fayemi wins governorship election
description: INEC declared Kayode Fayemi (APC) winner on 15 Jul 2018 with 197,459 votes against 178,121 for Kolapo Olusola of the PDP.
source: THISDAY: INEC Declares Fayemi Winner
notes_limitations: Wikipedia shows slightly different totals (197,462 / 177,927), and outlets disagree on how many LGAs each candidate won (11 to 13). Use INEC's declared result.

event_title: Kayode Fayemi begins second term
description: Fayose's term ended on 16 Oct 2018 and Fayemi, now in the APC, began a second term that ran to Oct 2022.
source: Wikipedia: Ayo Fayose
notes_limitations: Confirm swearing-in date with the state government.

event_title: Construction of Ekiti airport begins
description: Construction of the airport in Ado-Ekiti, later named the Ekiti Agro-Allied International Cargo Airport, began under Governor Fayemi.
source: ch-aviation: Ado Ekiti opens for first commercial flights
notes_limitations: Governor Oyebanji credits four administrations: Oni conceived it, Fayose acquired the site, Fayemi began construction and Oyebanji completed it.

event_title: College of Education, Ikere-Ekiti upgraded to BOUESTI
description: The Assembly passed and Governor Fayemi signed the bill upgrading the College of Education (est. 1977) into a university, later renamed Bamidele Olumilua University of Education, Science and Technology.
source: Wikipedia: College of Education, Ikere Ekiti
notes_limitations: Year is supported by Nigerian NewsDirect (Jan 2021, VC appointed). One listing gives 16 Oct 2020 as the upgrade date, citing the university site; unconfirmed.

event_title: Survey reports Ekiti among states with fewest out-of-school children
description: A 2022 government and UNICEF survey is reported to put Ekiti at about 2 percent of children out of school, second only to Imo.
source: Dubawa: Fact-checking Oyebanji's election broadcast claims
notes_limitations: Second-hand report. Find the underlying survey (likely NBS/UNICEF) and confirm the figure and year.

event_title: Biodun Oyebanji wins governorship election
description: Oyebanji (APC) was declared winner on 19 Jun 2022 with about 187,000 votes (53 percent), ahead of Segun Oni and Kolawole.
source: Wikipedia: 2022 Ekiti State gubernatorial election
notes_limitations: Confirm the final figures from INEC.

event_title: Oyebanji sworn in as governor
description: Biodun Oyebanji succeeded Kayode Fayemi as governor.
source: Wikipedia: List of governors of Ekiti State
notes_limitations: Confirm with the state government.

event_title: Ekiti airport ceremonially commissioned while unfinished
description: Governor Fayemi commissioned the airport in a ceremony shortly before leaving office; the state government of the day said the facility was still under construction.
source: SaharaReporters: Ekiti Government confirms airport still under construction (22 Oct 2022)
notes_limitations: Daily Trust dates the commissioning to Oct 2023, contradicting reports from 2022 and Fayemi's tenure ending Oct 2022. Confirm with an official source.

event_title: Ikogosi Warm Springs Resort placed under private concession
description: The state handed management of the resort to Glocient Hospitality Limited, a Cavista Holdings subsidiary, under a 15-year build-operate-transfer concession.
source: THISDAY: Glocient Hospitality Urges Tourists to Visit Ikogosi (22 Jul 2023)
notes_limitations: The article, dated July 2023, refers to a concession ceremony in 'October 2023', which cannot be right; facts.ng says 2022. Confirm the signing date with the Ministry of Tourism.

event_title: Federal Medical Centre Ido-Ekiti upgraded to teaching hospital
description: The federal government upgraded the Federal Medical Centre in Ido-Ekiti to a teaching hospital.
source: Wikipedia: Federal Medical Centre, Ido Ekiti
notes_limitations: The same page also mentions 2024 appointments to the teaching hospital board. Confirm the upgrade date with a federal source.

event_title: African Development Bank commits $80 million to Ekiti Knowledge Zone
description: AfDB announced an $80 million commitment to the EKZ project, including a 20-hectare green technology park and ICT training for over 19,000 young people.
source: African Development Bank press release
notes_limitations: Date is the press release date (22 Feb 2024); the formal approval date may differ.

event_title: Udiroko festival 2024: senators donate N110 million to Ado-Ekiti
description: At the 2024 Udiroko festival, Senate leaders donated N110 million toward Ado-Ekiti's development and Senate President Akpabio was installed as an honorary chief.
source: Tribune Online: Udiroko festival 2024
notes_limitations: Exact date not confirmed; the festival is held each August and the article is dated 6 Sep 2024.

event_title: 80-bed multipurpose hospital complex flagged off at EKSUTH
description: Governor Oyebanji flagged off construction of an 80-bed multipurpose medical building at the Ekiti State University Teaching Hospital, Ado-Ekiti.
source: Ekiti State Government: Gov. Oyebanji Flags Off Multipurpose 80 Bed Hospital Facility At EKSUTH
notes_limitations: Confirmed independently by Dubawa's fact-check. Completion status not yet checked.

event_title: NCAA approves commercial operations at Ekiti airport
description: The Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority granted a six-month approval for commercial operations at the Ado-Ekiti airport.
source: ch-aviation: Ado Ekiti opens for first commercial flights
notes_limitations: Month only. The state government also announced the approval.

event_title: First commercial flight lands at Ekiti Agro-Allied International Cargo Airport
description: United Nigeria Airlines operated the first commercial flight, connecting Ado-Ekiti with Abuja and Lagos. The state says it spent about N49.77 billion directly.
source: TheCable: Ekiti airport begins commercial flight operations
notes_limitations: Cost figure is the state government's own.

event_title: Sod turned for Ekiti Knowledge Zone
description: Vice President Kashim Shettima, representing President Tinubu, turned the sod for the Ekiti Knowledge Zone at Ago Araromi, Ado-Ekiti. The state projects up to 100,000 jobs.
source: Ekiti State Government: Ekiti Knowledge Zone 'll Be Nigeria's Innovation, Job Creation Hub
notes_limitations: Job projection is a government forecast. Date is the 'Tuesday' in the official report, matched to a 9 Jun 2026 news report.

event_title: Oyebanji re-elected: first consecutive-term win in state history
description: INEC declared Oyebanji winner with 319,224 votes to 40,543 (PDP) and 12,872 (ADC). He won all 16 LGAs. The ADC candidate alleged irregularities, which Oyebanji rejected.
source: Channels TV: INEC declares Oyebanji winner
notes_limitations: Election held 20 Jun; declared early on 21 Jun.

event_title: Udiroko festival 2026 celebrated in Ado-Ekiti
description: Ado-Ekiti marked its new-year festival, which tradition dates to about 1310 AD under Oba Awamaro, the first Ewi.
source: Channels TV: Ado-Ekiti celebrates Udiroko Festival
notes_limitations: Origin date (c.1310 AD) is traditional. See the Ekiti State Government's Udiroko article for the tradition.
